title: Per-Window Toolbar Strip
description:
Every window receives its own toolbar strip on the bottom (same as footer but floating and glassy like window options). Tools are now on window level. In the footer should only remain app mode wide commands.

Implementation: add a `toolbar` slot to `Window`/`WindowConfig` in ui/js/react/index.tsx, styled as a full-width floating glass strip at the bottom of the window body (windowOptions glass tier, no rounded corners), foldable with the same chrome pattern as WindowMeasuresChrome/WindowEngagementChrome, folded chip anchored bottom-left. Rewire framework/renderer/react/os-shell.tsx to source tools per window kind (toolNodesByKind via plugin.tools called per windowKindId) instead of one global activeToolNodes, pass each window its own ToolTree via the new toolbar slot, and strip the ToolTree/tools out of footerToolbar so the footer only keeps the app label item and the app-wide SyncAttachCard/sync tools. Update ui/styling/js/ui.css with a matching glass rule for the new data-slot, and extend Window.stories.tsx / Footer.stories.tsx and the existing test suites (framework/renderer/react/index.test.ts, in-source Window tests) accordingly. No rounded corners anywhere in the new/touched classes per repo design rule.
summary:
Fixed the row layout still growing taller and looking oversized when unfolded, per dev feedback ("expansion changes the height and not just grows to the right... too large").

Root cause: `windowToolbarBodyClass`/`windowEngagementBodyClass` used `p-tiny` (3 spacing units of padding on all four sides) added on top of already-h-medium-sized content (buttons/input), making the body taller than the fixed-height chrome button beside it. Combined with `items-stretch` on the row, that taller body forced the chrome to stretch to match, inflating the whole strip well past the intended single-row height.

Fix: `windowToolbarBodyClass` is now `h-medium` (fixed, matches the chrome exactly, never taller) with horizontal-only `px-single` padding — toolbars are always single-row, no vertical padding needed. `windowEngagementBodyClass` is now `min-h-medium` (at least one line, matching the chrome by default) with `justify-center` and horizontal-only `px-single` — still allowed to grow taller for Engagement's own optional status/options rows, but no longer padded taller than necessary for the common bare-input case. Both rows switched from `items-stretch` to `items-start` so the chrome button stays pinned at its natural `h-medium` size instead of being force-stretched whenever the body happens to be taller (relevant for Command's rare multi-row case; a no-op for Toolbar since its body is now always exactly `h-medium`).

Verified via the full ui-react vitest suite (199/208 passing, same 9 pre-existing unrelated tree-helper failures), and a clean lint run. Note: this file saw heavy concurrent edits from other sessions during this fix (line numbers shifted repeatedly mid-edit); the fix itself only touches the two class constants and the two `items-stretch`→`items-start` render sites, confirmed intact by direct grep after each conflict.
